author: ScraperCompany
description: 166+ live data tools for AI agents across travel and the open web: hotel rate calendars (up to 330 nights), booking-site vs own-website prices, Airbnb/Vrbo, Google Flights, guest reviews, car rentals, attractions, plus search, jobs, shopping, property, SEC filings and more. Connect with OAuth or an API key. Pick tool groups in the URL (default is 24 hotel/flight tools; /mcp/g/all is everything). Each tool states its credit cost; failed or empty calls are free.

tools.name: scrape_url
tools.title: Read a web page
tools.description: Fetch any public http(s) URL and return its content, as markdown unless format says otherwise, with the site's own status_code. render=true runs the page's JavaScript for JavaScript-built pages (wait_for: a CSS selector to wait for); premium=true uses the premium network for sites that block standard requests; country makes the request from that country. Private and internal addresses are refused. Costs 1 credit; 5 with render, 10 with premium, 75 with both. Non-2xx, blocked, failed and empty pages are free.

url.description: The page to fetch: an absolute `http://` or `https://` URL on port 80, 443, 8080 or 8443. Private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses, and hosts on the scrape denylist, are refused (422), as is any redirect to one; at most 5 redirects are followed.

format.description: markdown (default here), text, or html as served.

render.description: Run the page's JavaScript and return the DOM after `domcontentloaded` and any `wait_for`/`wait_ms`. Needed for pages that build their content with JavaScript. 5 credits instead of 1.

premium.description: Use the premium network from the first attempt, for sites that block standard requests. 10 credits (75 with `render`).

wait_for.description: CSS selector to wait for after `domcontentloaded` (attached to the DOM, visible or not), e.g. `#prices .row`. Never appearing within `timeout_s` is a 503 with Retry-After: retry, or allow more time. Needs `render`.

wait_ms.description: A further fixed wait, in milliseconds (0-10000), after the page and any `wait_for`. Needs `render`.
